Chapter 3: Growing Through Patience and Uncertainty.
You know that feeling when you just want answers—right now? Especially when something really matters to you. If you’re someone who creates, you’ve probably wrestled with questions like, “Is this any good? Will anyone care? Am I just wasting my time?” It’s so tempting to look for quick fixes, or to ask someone else for reassurance, hoping the uncertainty will just disappear.
But here’s the thing—real growth doesn’t work on your schedule. It’s not something you can pencil in or force to happen. It’s more like tending a garden than following a recipe. There are stretches where you’re just waiting, dealing with doubts, and sometimes, it feels like absolutely nothing is happening at all.
Imagine this: someone’s just finished a poem, a painting, maybe a song. They’re proud, but also a little anxious. They want to know if it’s good, if it matters. So, they show it to a friend, hoping for a little praise or maybe some helpful feedback. Sometimes, they get the encouragement they’re looking for. But more often, the response is vague or just... lukewarm. That uncertainty doesn’t really go away.
Most people find this uncertainty tough to sit with. They want clear feedback—a roadmap to success. But the truth is, the answers that matter most? Nobody else can give them to you. The only real way forward is to keep working, keep asking those questions, and accept that not everything will get solved right away.
Patience, then, becomes its own kind of discipline. It’s not about sitting back and doing nothing—it’s about waiting, trusting that the answers will come when they’re ready. The creative journey is full of false starts and dead ends, but every single one is a step toward something deeper.
Think about those small, everyday moments: someone sits down to write, but nothing comes. Frustration starts to build, and it’s tempting to just quit. But instead, they wait. Maybe they go for a walk, let their mind drift, and eventually, the words start to flow again. It’s not magic—it’s patience. It’s trusting the process, even when it doesn’t seem to make sense.
Over time, you start to realize that uncertainty isn’t a problem to be solved. It’s actually part of the journey. It’s what keeps your work alive, pushing you to keep searching and exploring. When the answers finally show up, they’re hard-won and deeply personal. No one else can hand them to you—you have to find them for yourself, through living.
Here’s what most people miss: the greatest growth happens right in those spaces between certainty and doubt. It’s in those moments of not knowing that real breakthroughs are born. That’s when your work becomes richer, more complex, and more true to life.
